To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cooling of proto quark stars with initial temperatures in range 40 MeV < T < 80 MeV is significantly delayed due to neutrino-trapping, and that the delay is of the order of the duration of long gamma-ray bursts.
the neutrino transport in the hot quark matter is very important for the cooling of the protoquark star.
the neutrino trapping (or neutrino opacity) is a very effective mechanism to delay the cooling of proto quark stars.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early cooling of hot protoquark stars.
the early cooling evolution and the neutrino transport of proto quark stars.
the influence of neutrino transport on the cooling of protoquark stars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutrino transport is not important for the early evolution of the protoquark star, and therefore the neutrinos do not play a role in the formation of the long gamma ray bursts.
neutrino trapping can delay the cooling of hot proto quarks stars to a neutrino transparency temperature of T_{trans} ~ 1.0 - 1.3 MeV by about a factor of 10.
the neutrino trapping is not the dominant factor for the cooling of protoquark stars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neutrino trapping is an important ingredient for the cooling evolution of hot PQS.
the neutrino trapping in the early evolution of hot PQS is an important cooling delay mechanism.
neutrinos are important for the cooling of PQS, but not for the duration of the gamma-ray burst.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cooling delay is not a consequence of the high initial temperatures but is due to the neutrino trapping.
the neutrino trapping effect is very important for the early evolution of PQS.
neutrino trapping can be a significant factor in the cooling evolution of proto quark stars.
